item.title: UK PM Burnham to meet business leaders to discuss growth
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet the bosses of several major companies on Monday to discuss his plans to generate economic growth, his office said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet the bosses of several major companies on Monday to discuss his plans to generate economic growth, his office said. Burnham will host a reception with the chief executives of companies including banks HSBC (HSBA.L) and Standard Chartered (STAN.L) , oil majors BP (BP.L) and Shell (SHEL.L) , and telecom firms BT (BT.L) and Vodafone (VOD.L) . He will say his plans for devolution can help deliver much-needed infrastructure and will look to support a culture shift to back innovation. The meeting with the bosses of Britain's biggest energy companies follows a report Burnham is set [USN:L8N4530WC TEXT:"to delay a decision"] on whether to bring the Shell-backed Jackdaw gas field online until after a parliamentary by-election next month. Ahead of the reception, he will hold a roundtable with British entrepreneurs from the fields of fintech, AI, clean energy and advanced manufacturing. Burnham's finance minister John Healey last week used [USN:L1N44Z06Z TEXT:"his first major speech"] since taking office to set out a brighter vision for the economy before an annual budget where he faces tough tax and spending choices.

item.title: Vikings QB Kyler Murray (concussion) ruled out vs. Packers
item.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was ruled out of Sunday's game against the visiting Green Bay Packers after suffering a concussion on scramble in the first quarter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was ruled out of Sunday's game against the visiting Green Bay Packers after suffering a concussion on scramble in the first quarter. Murray took a hard hit to the side of his head and had his helmet knocked off as he slid short of the first-down marker with 6:10 to go in the opening quarter. He stayed on the turf while medical staff attended to him. Eventually, Murray got to his feet and walked to the locker room without assistance. The team announced in the second quarter that Murray had been ruled out for the remainder of the game. Packers safety Javon Bullard was penalized 15 yards for unnecessary roughness on the play. Carson Wentz replaced Murray at quarterback. The Vikings made headlines earlier this month when they named the veteran Wentz as their No. 2 quarterback ahead of former first-round pick JJ McCarthy. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brandon Lowe's pinch-hit heroics help Pirates evade sweep by Cubs
item.description: Brandon Lowe drove in two runs with a pinch-hit single in the sixth inning as the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Chicago Cubs 4-3 Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Lowe drove in two runs with a pinch-hit single in the sixth inning as the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Chicago Cubs 4-3 Sunday. The Cubs (83-67) fell into a tie with the Phillies for the first National League wild-card spot. Philadelphia beat Atlanta 9-4 Sunday. Chicago hosts the Braves in a three-game series starting Monday. The Pirates (75-75) avoided the sweep with the win. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (8-5) gave up seven hits and four runs in 5 1/3 innings. The southpaw walked two and struck out three in 88 pitches. Pirates starter Bubba Chandler (8-9) gave up five hits and three runs in 5 1/3 innings. The right-hander walked four and struck out three in 90 pitches. Mason Montgomery picked up his 13th save with a scoreless ninth inning. The Pirates started the scoring in the first when Konnor Griffin led off with a single and Oneil Cruz walked. Bryan Reynolds singled in Griffin for a 1-0 lead. Chandler only allowed one Cub to reach second base through 4 2/3 innings before Chicago broke through. Pedro Ramirez started the rally with a two-out walk, setting up Miguel Amaya for a two-run home run to left to put the Cubs in front 2-1. The Pirates fought back in the sixth when Reynolds walked to lead off and Rafael Flores Jr. singled. Nick Gonzales followed with a long drive to right over the head of Seiya Suzuki. The ball was lost in the ivy for a ground-rule double that tied the game 2-2. Boyd struck out Ryan O'Hearn for the first out of the inning, and Aaron Civale replaced him to face Jake Mangum. Mangum walked and Lowe followed with his single to center, scoring Flores and Gonzales to make it 4-2 Pirates. The Cubs cut it to one in the sixth when Michael Busch singled with one out and Alex Bregman doubled to left. Ian Happ walked to load the bases and Busch scored when Nico Hoerner grounded out. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alec Burlseon gives Cards win over White Sox with one swing
item.description: Alec Burleson hit a go-ahead, bases-clearing double in the bottom of the sixth inning and Michael McGreevy pitched six effective innings Sunday afternoon for the host St. Louis Cardinals in a 3-1 victory over the Chicago White Sox.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alec Burleson hit a go-ahead, bases-clearing double in the bottom of the sixth inning and Michael McGreevy pitched six effective innings Sunday afternoon for the host St. Louis Cardinals in a 3-1 victory over the Chicago White Sox. Chicago put its first two runners aboard in the ninth and loaded the bases with two outs, but Colson Montgomery flied to medium center field against George Soriano. Montgomery also made a key error earlier that set up Burleson's big hit. Reaching the postseason remains unlikely for the Cardinals (74-76), but they made a definite impact on the American League Central race after taking two of three from the first-place White Sox. A day after mounting a ninth-inning comeback to stop a four-game losing streak and increase their division lead, the White Sox (76-73) saw the Cleveland Guardians creep within a half-game of first place after beating the Minnesota Twins on Sunday. The White Sox, who have dropped 10 of 14, head to Cleveland for a three-game showdown starting Monday night. White Sox rookie right-hander David Sandlin retired his first 16 batters before Nathan Church blooped a single to right with one out in the bottom of the sixth. The No. 9 hitter, Masyn Winn, followed with another bloop single to left, which brought White Sox pitching coach Zach Bove to the mound for a meeting. Sandlin responded by striking out Bryan Torres for the second out, but Ivan Herrera reached to load the bases when Montgomery booted a routine-looking grounder to short. White Sox manager Will Venable called on left-hander Chris Murphy to face Burleson. Burleson, a lefty who is much weaker against same-sided pitchers, did a great job fighting off a pitch on his hands, dumping a three-run double inside the line in right. It gave him 109 RBIs, putting him in the major league lead at the time. Sandlin (2-2) allowed three unearned runs and two hits to go with five strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings. He's in his third stint this season with the White Sox, having been recalled from Triple-A after Saturday's comeback win. The White Sox continued to struggle with runners in scoring position, going 0-for-7 and stranding seven overall. They failed to add any runs after Sam Antonacci led off the sixth with a triple. McGreevy (7-9) allowed a run, three hits and three walks with six strikeouts after posting a 6.26 ERA over his previous nine starts. Gordon Graceffo struck out three in two scoreless innings, and Soriano converted his fourth save despite the traffic. The Cardinals came in 7 1/2 games back in the NL Wild Card chase. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc seen winning by one seat, election authority projects
item.description: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc is projected to win a one-seat majority in Sunday's vote for parliament, the election authority said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc is projected to win a one-seat majority in Sunday's vote for parliament, the election authority said. The bloc, headed by Social Democrats party leader Magdalena Andersson, was expected to win 175 seats in the 349-seat parliament, the agency projected based on votes from 4,853 of Sweden's 6,312 election districts. The right-wing governing bloc was seen winning 174 seats.

item.title: Ferran Torres scores again as PSG earn first Ligue 1 win of the season
item.description: Champions Paris St Germain won their first match of the new Ligue 1 season with World Cup winner Ferran Torres keeping up his red-hot goalscoring form with the only goal of the game in a 1-0 win at Stade Brestois on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Champions Paris St Germain won their first match of the new Ligue 1 season with World Cup winner Ferran Torres keeping up his red-hot goalscoring form with the only goal of the game in a 1-0 win at Stade Brestois on Sunday. Torres took five minutes to put PSG ahead, picking up a loose ball in midfield, passing to Joao Neves, then Ousmane Dembele whose back heel into Torres’ path gave the Spaniard time to bend a low shot into the corner. He has now netted six goals in five outings since moving to the European champions after scoring the winner for Spain in July’s World Cup final against Argentina in New York. PSG had made a slow start to the new league campaign, with two points from their opening three fixtures. Brest had an opportunity to earn a share of the spoils with Kamory Doumbia hitting the outside of the upright after a defensive slip by Nuno Mendes gave him a clear sight of goal. Doumbia also had a header in the second half denied by a sharp save from PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov. Brest's players all wore the name ‘King’ on the back of their shirts in tribute to coach Eric ‘King’ Roy, who died of cancer aged 58 in June. LILLE GO TOP Earlier on Sunday, last season’s runners-up RC Lens fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 at promoted Le Mans while Lille went top of the standings after an easy 2-0 triumph over Troyes. The victory put Lille top with 10 points from four matches, ahead of Monaco and Rennes on goal difference. Lens, who had lost two of their opening three fixtures of the campaign, moved to four points while Le Mans are still looking for their first win of the season. Le Mans looked in command in the first half at Stade Marie-Marvingt after Adil Bourabaa headed home a rebound after Louis Mafouta’s effort bounced back off the crossbar in the 32nd minute, and then a quick counter-attack allowed Lucas Calodat to double their advantage in the 44th minute. Lens pulled one back from tall Senegalese striker Abdallah Sima in stoppage time before the break, and then equalised with another header, this time from substitute Franjo Ivanovic six minutes into the second half. Lille bounced back after their home loss to Real Betis in the Champions League in midweek to beat Troyes in a one-sided encounter at Stade Pierre-Mauroy. Fullback Tiago Santos scored for a second time this season as he curled a first-time, right-footed shot into the far top corner. Ethan Mbappe, sent off in the Champions League in midweek, came on as a substitute to add the second goal in stoppage time.

item.title: Guardians creep closer to AL Central lead by hammering Twins
item.description: Steven Kwan, Jo Adell and Travis Bazzana hit home runs in the Cleveland Guardians' 9-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Sunday in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Steven Kwan, Jo Adell and Travis Bazzana hit home runs in the Cleveland Guardians' 9-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Sunday in Minneapolis. Kwan was 3-for-4 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs while Bazzana added a walk, three RBIs and two runs and Adell scored two and drove in two for the Guardians (76-74), who moved within a half-game of the American League Central-leading Chicago White Sox. Trevor Larnach homered and doubled and Luke Keaschall added two hits for the Twins (70-79), who have lost three of their last four. Tanner Bibee (6-15) got the win by giving up two runs and four hits in 6 2/3 innings with two walks and seven strikeouts. Minnesota starter Joe Ryan (6-10) allowed four runs on seven hits in four innings with a walk and a strikeout. Kwan put the Guardians on top with a leadoff home run. He hit Ryan's 1-0 four-seam fastball into the overhang above the right field wall for his third homer of the year. Adell's home run leading off the third made it 2-0. He blasted Ryan's 0-1 four-seam fastball an estimated 451 feet into the third deck in left field. The exit velocity was 116.8 mph on Adell's 21st homer. Kody Clemens' two-out, run-scoring double in the bottom of the third put the Twins on the board for a 2-1 game. The Guardians responded with two in the fourth on Kwan's RBI double and Bazzana's two-out, run-producing single to stretch their lead to 4-1. Bazzana's two-run homer off Travis Adams made it 6-1 in the sixth. His 12th home run sailed into the right-center-field stands. Larnarch's 13th home run leading off the seventh pulled the Twins within 6-2. But Cleveland added three in the ninth on Adell's RBI double, a sacrifice fly by Nathaniel Lowe and a run-scoring double from Angel Martinez. Minnesota first baseman Royce Lewis left the game in the fifth with left shoulder soreness. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eugenio Suarez's homer, late plays lift Reds past Brewers
item.description: Elly De La Cruz scored the go-ahead run on Tyler Stephenson's sacrifice fly in the eighth inning, lifting the visiting Cincinnati Reds to a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Elly De La Cruz scored the go-ahead run on Tyler Stephenson's sacrifice fly in the eighth inning, lifting the visiting Cincinnati Reds to a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday afternoon. Cincinnati's Eugenio Suarez launched a three-run homer in the sixth inning, marking his second homer in as many games. De La Cruz singled off Abner Uribe (5-3) to lead off the eighth inning and advanced to third on rookie Sal Stewart's base hit. Stephenson stepped up two batters later and lofted a sacrifice fly to right field to plate De La Cruz to give the Reds a 4-3 lead. De La Cruz and Stewart each had two of the Reds' eight hits to help the Reds (70-79) salvage the finale of a 1-5 road trip. Brandon Williamson (4-4) allowed one run on two hits in four innings in relief of Chase Burns. Brock Burke bridged the gap to Emilio Pagan, who retired the side in the ninth inning to secure his 23rd save of the season. Joey Ortiz belted a two-run homer in the second inning and Jake Bauers went deep to lead off the seventh for the Brewers (93-57), who saw their five-game winning streak come to a halt. Milwaukee starter Robert Gasser allowed his third hit with a leadoff single to De La Cruz in the sixth inning. Antonio Senzatela relieved Gasser and permitted a single to rookie Sal Stewart before seeing Suarez deposit a 0-1 sinker over the wall in right-center field to stake Cincinnati to a 3-2 lead. Suarez's homer was his 24th of the season. Bauers sent a 1-0 fastball from Williamson over the wall in right-center field to forge a 3-3 tie. Bauers' homer was his 26th of the season and third in his last six games. Christian Yelich worked a one-out walk in the second inning before Ortiz deposited a 2-1 fastball from Burns over the wall in center field to open the scoring. The homer was Ortiz's ninth of the season. Uribe permitted one run on two hits in one inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: Agustin Ramirez blasts walk-off HR as Marlins take series from Dodgers
item.description: Pinch hitter Agustin Ramirez hit a two-run, walk-off homer in the ninth to give the Miami Marlins a 6-4 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Agustin Ramirez hit a two-run, walk-off homer in the ninth to give the Miami Marlins a 6-4 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday. Miami entered the eighth inning losing 3-0, but pulled within one on a two-run single from Otto Lopez. The Marlins entered the ninth behind 4-2 with ex-Marlins pitcher Tanner Scott on the mound to close it out. Xavier Edwards' infield single, Jakob Marsee's bunt hit and Javier Sanoja's softly hit two-run double down the left field line tied the score 4-4 with nobody out. Los Angeles brought in Brock Stewart to gain the platoon advantage against Ramirez, who got a 94-mph fastball down the middle and belted it 407 feet to left center. Miami (74-76) won for just the third time in 10 contests, but the hosts won the three-game series as Los Angeles (90-59) dropped its second straight game after winning eight in a row. The loss ruined a great performance by Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula, who slugged a three-run homer for his first MLB hit and doubled off the wall. The 21-year-old outfielder, who made his MLB debut on Friday, finished the game 2-for-2 with a walk. The Marlins played a video tribute after the first inning for Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas, who plans to retire after this season. Rojas, 37, played for the Marlins from 2015-22. Rojas went 1-for-3 on Sunday, but he banged his right shoulder in the eighth when he made a diving attempt at Joe Mack's ground-ball single. After a brief delay, Rojas remained in the game before leaving for a pinch hitter in the ninth. Dodgers starter Emmet Sheehan allowed two hits and one walk over six scoreless innings. He struck out five and was in line for the win before his bullpen caved. Los Angeles took a 3-0 lead in the fourth as Will Smith doubled, Kyle Tucker walked and De Paula unloaded on a 98-mph Eury Perez fastball that he pulled 416 feet to right. Miami scored twice in the eighth against reliever Edgardo Henriquez as Mack and Esteury Ruiz singled and Heriberto Hernandez walked to load the bases. With two outs, Lopez singled off a 100.4-mph fastball to cut the deficit to 3-2. Scott came in and struck out Griffin Conine on three pitches, including two swings on pitches well out of the strike zone. Los Angeles extended its lead to 4-2 in the ninth as Alex Freeland singled, stole second and scored on Mookie Betts' double. --Field Level Media

item.title: Caleb Williams, Bears put up 59 on Panthers in record-setting opener
item.description: Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more and the Chicago Bears pulled away for a 59-37 victory against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more and the Chicago Bears pulled away for a 59-37 victory against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. In the teams' season opener, D'Andre Swift scored three touchdown runs and rushed for 124 yards on 18 carries for Chicago. Williams completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and added 65 rushing yards. Kyle Monangai gained 100 yards on 10 carries, including a 61-yard TD. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw two of his three touchdown passes to Jalen Coker. Young was 23 of 37 for 361 yards with one interception. Coker made eight catches for 138 yards. Chuba Hubbard scored touchdowns on a run and a reception. The Panthers pulled even at 31-31 on Hubbard's 2-yard run with 9:02 left in the third quarter. From there, the Bears posted the next three touchdowns on runs by Swift (1 yard) and Monangai and Williams' 1-yard pass to Jahdae Walker. Later, Swift found the end zone from 28 yards out. Cairo Santos' 40-yard field goal for the Bears and Ryan Fitzgerald's 44-yarder for the Panthers left the teams tied at 24-24 late in the first half. Williams rambled 29 yards with 22 seconds left for a 31-24 lead. Chicago had 315 yards of first-half total offense. The points parade began early. After the Bears fumbled two snaps into the game, the Panthers went 42 yards for a touchdown on their first possession. Young threw 4 yards to Hubbard for the score. Chicago pulled even when Williams scrambled around the left side for a 9-yard touchdown to complete a nine-play drive. Swift ran 1 yard for a score later in the first quarter for the Bears' first lead. He had 65 first-quarter rushing yards. Chicago took over at the Carolina 41 following a Panthers punt and penalty. Cole Kmet's 22-yard reception produced the touchdown. Three plays later, the Panthers were in the end zone on Young's 51-yard pass to Jalen Coker. The Bears gambled on a fourth-down play at their own 21, failing to pick up 1 yard as Carolina took over and converted when Young raced 7 yards for a touchdown. The score was 21-21 just over 21 minutes into the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lions roar on offense before edging Saints 31-30 in OT
item.description: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 156 yards and two touchdowns, Jared Goff threw two touchdown passes to Amon-Ra St. Brown and the host Detroit Lions held off the New Orleans Saints 31-30 in overtime Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 156 yards and two touchdowns, Jared Goff threw two touchdown passes to Amon-Ra St. Brown and the host Detroit Lions held off the New Orleans Saints 31-30 in overtime Sunday afternoon. Goff passed for 206 yards and the Lions had to stop a two-point conversion on the final play to prevail. Detroit got the ball first in overtime and Goff threw a 4-yard TD pass to St. Brown for a 31-24 lead with 5:04 remaining. Tyler Shough drove the Saints to his 8-yard touchdown pass to Noah Fant, but his two-point conversion pass was incomplete in the back of the end zone. Shough recovered from three turnovers to pass for 410 yards and three touchdowns, including the 9-yard strike to Juwan Johnson late in regulation that forced OT. Chris Olave hauled in 10 receptions for 182 yards. On the first play of the third quarter, Derrick Barnes intercepted Shough, giving the Lions the ball at the Saints' 41. Seven plays later, Gibbs ran 1 yard for his second touchdown and a 14-0 lead. On New Orleans' next possession, Shough fumbled while being sacked by Roger McCreary and DJ Wonnum recovered at the Saints' 25. Three plays later, Goff threw a 19-yard touchdown pass to St. Brown for a 21-0 lead. On the first play of the ensuing possession, Shough connected with Olave on a 47-yard completion, which soon led to Kendre Miller's 8-yard touchdown run. New Orleans forced a three-and-out and drove to Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele that trimmed the lead to 21-14 at the end of the third quarter. The Saints scored for a third straight possession when Daniel Carlson's 28-yard field goal pulled them within four points midway through the fourth quarter. Jake Bates' 23-yard field goal pushed the lead to 24-17 with 2:32 left. Shough helped New Orleans drive 75 yards in eight plays and just 1:25 of game time, ending with his TD pass to Johnson to tie the score with 1:07 left. Goff directed a 13-play, 89-yard drive in the first quarter that ended with Gibbs' 1-yard touchdown run. The 7-0 lead held up through the end of the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Phillies use seven-run eighth inning to stymie Braves
item.description: Alec Bohm's two-run double in the eighth inning sparked a seven-run rally and helped the visiting Philadelphia Phillies defeat the Atlanta Braves 9-4 on Sunday and salvage a contest from their three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alec Bohm's two-run double in the eighth inning sparked a seven-run rally and helped the visiting Philadelphia Phillies defeat the Atlanta Braves 9-4 on Sunday and salvage a contest from their three-game series. Philadelphia (83-67) cut Atlanta's lead in the National League East to five games with the victory. Atlanta's magic number to win the division remains seven. The Braves (88-62) won the season series 9-4. Facing reliever Dylan Lee (6-1) with the score tied 2-2, the Phillies had runners at second and third when Bohm drove a two-out liner to center field to score Bryce Harper and Trea Turner. Bryson Stott and J.T. Realmuto followed with run-scoring singles that stretched the lead to 6-2. Kyle Schwarber added a two-run single and Trea Turner singled home a run. Realmuto and Stott each had three of the team's 16 hits and were among six players with multiple hits. Neither starter figured in the decision. Philadelphia's Andrew Painter pitched five strong innings and allowed one run on six hits and four walks, striking out three. Atlanta's Grant Holmes was able to pitch only four innings, allowing two runs on five hits and two walks. The Braves scored a run in the first. Michael Harris II led off with a single, advanced to third on Matt Olson's single and scored on Drake Baldwin's sacrifice fly. It was Baldwin's fourth RBI of the series. But Philadelphia scored twice in the second inning to take the lead. Realmuto hit a two-run homer, his 11th, that carried 405 feet into the left field seats. Atlanta first baseman Olson saved a run with his glove in the fifth inning. With runners on the corners, Kyle Schwarber grounded sharply to Olson, who stepped on the bag, checked the runner at third and threw out Justin Crawford at second base. The Braves tied the game in the seventh against reliever Jose Alvarado (4-3), the winning pitcher. Harris singled, took second on a wild pitch and scored on Olson's one-out single. It ended a nine-game scoreless streak for Alvarado. Olson, who went 3-for-5, added a two-run homer in the ninth inning, his 39th. --Field Level Media

item.title: VAR got goal award wrong in Manchester derby, says ref's body
item.description: The video assistant referee (VAR) was wrong to allow Erling Haaland's decisive goal in Manchester City's 1-0 win over Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, refereeing body Pro Ref said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The video assistant referee (VAR) was wrong to allow Erling Haaland's decisive goal in [USN:L6N45507B TEXT:"Manchester City's 1-0 win over Manchester United"] at Old Trafford on Sunday, refereeing body Pro Ref said in a statement. Haaland's strike on the hour mark was initially disallowed for offside but was allowed to stand after a VAR review found him to be onside. However, Pro Ref said the VAR failed to recognise the likely impact of his teammate Enzo Fernandez, who attempted to head the ball from an offside position. “The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position," the statement said. “In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review. “Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was angry at the decision as his side slumped to a derby defeat. "I just don't get it, I really don't get it, I can't understand how we're trying to help referees, putting so many layers behind them, so many people, bodies and screens, and they can't make the right decision," he told [USN:L6N45507T TEXT:"a post-match media conference"].

item.title: Deshaun Watson done after Week 1 disaster? Browns to 'watch the tape'
item.description: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken shielded quarterback Deshaun Watson from taking the blame alone for a 34-10 loss at Jacksonville on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken shielded quarterback Deshaun Watson from taking the blame alone for a 34-10 loss at Jacksonville on Sunday. "I'd rather just speak about today, because I haven't had time to even look at the tape," Monken said. Watson was intercepted on the first drive of the game, and Cleveland fell into a 31-0 hole early in the third quarter. The Browns' lone touchdown of the game, a 46-yard pass from Watson to Denzel Boston, came with 1:52 left to play. Watson started Sunday in his first game in almost two years. He was named the starter for Week 1 following a quarterback competition in training camp with Shedeur Sanders. "I didn't take this job to lose, OK," Monken said. "We're going to analyze everything how we do, how we coach, starting with me. How we do it offensively, defensively. Deshaun is part of that, always has been, always will be, as our quarterbacks will be. "It would be unfair for me to really comment on any one given player. It's never as bad as you think. And it's never as good as you think." The Browns (0-1) are at Tampa Bay (0-1) next week. Monken disagreed with the postgame press conference assessment that Watson was "tentative." But according to NFL Next Gen Stats, Watson was 1 of 5 for 20 yards with one interception on passes that traveled at least 10 yards in the air in the first half while Cleveland dug a 24-0 hole. "He let that ball rip that was an interception. He let it rip. I think he let it rip," Monken said. Watson credited the Jaguars for "making the plays we didn't." "We just couldn't get our rhythm back," Watson said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jonathan Aranda keys offensive outburst as Rays rout Astros
item.description: Jonathan Aranda homered twice with three RBIs, starter Freddy Peralta twirled five no-hit innings, and the Tampa Bay Rays completed their majors-best 15th series sweep Sunday by pummeling the Houston Astros 14-4 in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jonathan Aranda homered twice with three RBIs, starter Freddy Peralta twirled five no-hit innings, and the Tampa Bay Rays completed their majors-best 15th series sweep Sunday by pummeling the Houston Astros 14-4 in St. Petersburg, Fla. Falling a homer shy of the cycle, Victor Mesa Jr. was 3-for-5 with three runs and two RBIs. Richie Palacios was 2-for-4 with a three-run homer and scored twice, while Nick Fortes went deep for American League East-leading Tampa Bay (90-59). The Rays posted 15 hits and were 4-for-9 with runners in scoring position. Winning his fourth straight start, Peralta (9-11) fanned four and walked three in his five innings. He left with the Rays up 11-0. Isaac Paredes, Nick Allen and Nelson Velazquez homered for the Astros (75-75), who had only four hits and are 2-6 in the past eight games. In a season-shortest start of three innings, Hayden Wesneski (5-2) surrendered seven runs on six hits, but four markers were unearned. He struck out two and walked two. Batting cleanup in the first inning, Mesa extended his hitting streak to nine games with a triple to right to score Yandy Diaz and Junior Caminero, who had singled and doubled, respectively. Chandler Simpson's groundout made it 3-0. Peralta walked the bases loaded in the third, and Paredes hit a hard grounder that was fielded by Caminero. The third baseman took a couple of steps into foul territory and bounced a throw that first baseman Aranda awkwardly secured for the final out. The Rays made it 7-0 with four unearned runs in the third after a crucial two-out error by Houston shortstop Jeremy Pena, who dropped an easy, shallow popup as he jogged out to left field to score Mesa. Palacios followed with a high three-run homer to right for his 10th long ball and the touchdown lead. Aranda made it 8-0 in the fourth with an opposite-field solo shot, and Simpson's RBI single scored Mesa for his third run. In the fifth, Fortes drilled a two-run shot, his fifth, as the home side pulled ahead 11-0. Paredes spoiled the no-hit bid with a one-out homer to left, his 21st, in the sixth. Diaz (2-for-5, two runs, RBI) singled in Palacios in the seventh before Aranda hit homer No. 21. Allen and Velazquez rounded out the scoring by stroking homers in the eighth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nationals rally late to sweep Angels
item.description: Jacob Young doubled in the go-ahead run during a four-run eighth as the host Washington Nationals rallied to complete a three-game sweep of the Los Angeles Angels with a 6-5 victory on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jacob Young doubled in the go-ahead run during a four-run eighth as the host Washington Nationals rallied to complete a three-game sweep of the Los Angeles Angels with a 6-5 victory on Sunday afternoon. Daylen Lile, CJ Abrams, Yohandy Morales and James Wood provided two hits apiece for Washington (70-81) as Erik Tolman (1-1) collected his first major league win in relief. Jack Sinclair handled the ninth for his first big-league save. Moises Ballesteros and Zach Neto homered and Mike Trout doubled and walked twice for Los Angeles (56-93), which finished 3-6 on its nine-game, 11-day trip. Luke Murphy (0-3) allowed four runs on four hits in his inning of relief. Los Angeles took a 1-0 lead in the fourth inning when Ballesteros smashed his ninth home run, a 407-foot drive to center. The Angels extended the lead to 2-0 in the fifth when Neto hit his 26th home run, a 440-foot drive into the bleachers in center. Washington parlayed three hits and a hit batter into two runs in the sixth to forge a 2-2 tie. Abrams started the rally by hustling for a double and scoring on a Morales single to center. Lile followed with a single and Keibert Ruiz was hit by a pitch to load the bases. Morales scored the tying run on a fielder's choice by pinch hitter Brady House. Los Angeles scored two runs without a hit to take a 4-2 lead in the eighth. Neto and Wade Meckler walked and it appeared Tolman would get out of the jam when Vaughn Grissom hit a double-play grounder to short, but Abrams mishandled the ball for an error to load the bases. Neto scored on a wild pitch and Ballesteros followed with a sacrifice fly. Washington answered with four runs in the bottom half of the inning highlighted by an RBI triple by Lile off the wall in right center, a pinch-hit RBI single by Jorbit Vivas to tie it, 4-4, and Young's double into the gap in left center. The Angels pulled within a run in the ninth when Josh Lowe led off with a double and scored on a groundout by Christian Moore. Sinclair struck out Neto to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blue Jays power past Orioles, move to .500
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays hit back-to-back-to-back home runs in the fifth inning Sunday and went on to defeat the visiting Baltimore Orioles 8-1.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Toronto Blue Jays hit back-to-back-to-back home runs in the fifth inning Sunday and went on to defeat the visiting Baltimore Orioles 8-1. George Springer, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Kazuma Okamoto homered in succession against Trevor Rogers (10-10) in the rubber match of a three-game series between teams chasing a playoff berth in the American League. Guerrero was 4-for-5 with a double and two singles to go with his home run, which was only his ninth of the season and first at home. Springer also had a double and four RBIs. Toronto (75-75) leads the season series 6-4. That is the first tiebreaker for a playoff berth. Baltimore (72-78) went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 13 runners. Toronto starter Dylan Cease (11-5) struck out three batters in a row in the first inning after the Orioles loaded the bases on two walks and a single. Toronto took a 1-0 lead in the second. Charles McAdoo led off with a single to left and scored on a one-out double by Andres Gimenez on a flare that tipped off the glove of third baseman Christian Encarnacion-Strand. The Orioles tied the game in the fifth. Dylan Beavers led off with a double into the right-field corner and scored on Pete Alonso's bloop single down the right-field line. It was Alonso's 100th RBI of the season. Cease allowed one run, four hits and five walks and struck out nine in five innings. Toronto regained the lead in the bottom of the fifth when Springer clubbed a two-out homer to right on a 1-0 changeup. Guerrero followed by belting a 3-2 sweeper to left, which brought a huge reaction from the crowd. Okamoto was next to homer when lofted a 3-2 fastball to left. It was his 32nd homer and a Blue Jays rookie-record 85th RBI. Toronto's Braydon Fisher replaced Ricky Tiedemann with runners at the corners and two out in the sixth and retired Alonso on a called third strike. Rogers completed six innings, allowing four runs, seven hits and one walk with five strikeouts. Baltimore's Yaramil Hiraldo walked Brett Bateman with the bases loaded in the eighth to extend Toronto's lead. Cam Sanders took over and Beavers misplayed Springer's drive to left into a three-run double. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ravens ride Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers to 41-23 win at Indy
item.description: Derrick Henry scored three touchdowns and powered the Ravens past the Colts 41-23 in Indianapolis on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Derrick Henry scored three touchdowns and powered the Ravens past the Colts 41-23 in Indianapolis on Sunday. Henry had 144 rushing yards and buoyed Baltimore's offense in the second half after injuries knocked wide receivers Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane out. Flowers (hamstring) had five receptions for a career-high 150 yards before he was ruled out. Lane (wrist), who had one catch and a TD overturned by an offensive penalty, left in the third quarter. Baltimore's offense ran in overdrive early and the Ravens outgained the Colts 506-251. Lamar Jackson had 324 yards passing with a touchdown pass to Flowers and ran for a score. Colts running back Jonathan Taylor had 121 yards from scrimmage and ran for 98 yards on 19 carries with two touchdowns. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (19 of 31, 166 yards, one TD) was under pressure until his final snap. The Ravens had an interception, two sacks and 10 QB hits. Jones rushed the Colts down the field and found Tyler Warren for a 9-yard TD with 10 minutes to play, but the Ravens came back with Tyler Loop's 45-yard field goal for a 41-23 advantage with 4:09 to go. Ravens coach Jesse Minter won in his debut as a head coach while the Colts fell to 1-8-1 in regular-season openers the past 10 years. Without Flowers and Lane, the Ravens lulled the Colts to sleep with a heavy dose of Henry in the third. Jackson went over 300 passing yards with a 53-yard throw lofted to Chris Moore to the Indianapolis 19. Henry did the rest, capped by a 3-yard run for his third rushing touchdown, stretching Baltimore's lead to 38-16 early in the fourth. With under five minutes left in the first half, Laiatu Latu's sack and forced fumble to set the Colts up at the Ravens' 15. Taylor ran in untouched from 3 yards out to whittle the deficit to 28-13. Flowers left the Colts in the dust on a 54-yard touchdown in the second quarter. It was his fourth catch for 138 yards with more than six minutes left in the second quarter. Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey ripped the ball away from Taylor. Henry's second TD of the game, a 32-yard romp off left tackle, made it a 28-6 game. Ravens first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's debut was a smashing success. Baltimore scored two touchdowns on its first nine plays (10 including a penalty) and led 14-6 only 11 minutes into the game. Roquan Smith intercepted Jones to give the Ravens only 31 yards to paydirt, which Baltimore covered in six plays. Henry cut back a stretch running play designed to go right and shuffled into the end zone untouched from 4 yards out for a 14-6 lead. Henry's 123rd career touchdown pulled him even with Marcus Allen for third on the all-time list, then he passed Allen on his second score in the second quarter. He added TD No. 3 in the first minute of the fourth quarter. Only LaDainian Tomlinson and Emmitt Smith have more career rushing touchdowns in NFL history. Baltimore's first play from scrimmage was Jackson's 49-yard pass to Flowers to the Indianapolis 2. Jackson sprinted to the left pylon for a touchdown on a designed run two plays later, responding to the Colts' opening-drive touchdown run by Taylor. Ravens cornerback T.J. Tampa was ruled out in the first quarter with a knee injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Manchester City hammer Aston Villa to go top of WSL
item.description: Reigning champions Manchester City thumped Aston Villa 4-1 away on Sunday to leave them top of the Women's Super League as the only team with two wins from their opening two games of the season.
item.dc:creator: Philip O'connor
item.content:encoded: Reigning champions Manchester City thumped Aston Villa 4-1 away on Sunday to leave them top of the Women's Super League as the only team with two wins from their opening two games of the season. Defender Jade Rose opened the scoring in the 14th minute and Mary Fowler added a second 15 minutes later to put City 2-0 up and cruising, but an Amalie Vangsgaard goal sent the home side into the break 2-1 down. Villa battled to hang on but Bunny Shaw netted in the 74th minute to break their resistance, and a stoppage-time own goal completed the rout as City continued their perfect start to the season. Earlier in the afternoon, Birmingham City and Brighton & Hove Albion drew 2-2 to give each side their first point of the season, while a Leighanne Robe own goal gave Everton a 1-0 win over Charlton Athletic at home. Everton's Merseyside rivals Liverpool were also at home, where they came back from a goal down to grab a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur, Aurelie Csillag coming off the bench to cancel out a Sam Kerr own goal. Crystal Palace followed up their victory last week against Everton with a scoreless draw away to Arsenal, while on Saturday, big-spending London City Lionesses were brought back down to earth after their opening-day win over Manchester United when they were beaten 2-1 away to West Ham United.

item.title: Vintage Josh Allen game lifts Bills over Texans in back-and-forth affair
item.description: Josh Allen accounted for four touchdowns and tossed the decisive 34-yard scoring pass to Joshua Palmer with 1:36 remaining as the Buffalo Bills won in Houston for the first time in 20 years with a wild 36-31 victory over the Texans in the season opener for both teams on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Josh Allen accounted for four touchdowns and tossed the decisive 34-yard scoring pass to Joshua Palmer with 1:36 remaining as the Buffalo Bills won in Houston for the first time in 20 years with a wild 36-31 victory over the Texans in the season opener for both teams on Sunday afternoon. Allen completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns and added two rushing scores while winning in Houston for the first time in five career attempts, including the postseason. The touchdown throw to Palmer capped a seven-play, 96-yard drive. Houston had one last chance at overcoming the deficit and reached the Buffalo 9-yard line. But on third-and-goal from the 18, Greg Rousseau sacked Houston's CJ Stroud and forced a fumble that teammate Terrel Bernard recovered at the Bills' 24 with nine seconds left to seal it. Dalton Kincaid had five receptions for 130 yards and DJ Moore had five catches for 100 yards and one touchdown in his Buffalo debut. Tyler Bass kicked three field goals and Rousseau had two sacks as the Bills won in Joe Brady's first game as head coach. David Montgomery rushed for two touchdowns and caught another in his Texans debut, while Stroud completed 26 of 38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns, including one to Nico Collins. Buffalo's winning excursion began at its own 4-yard line with 3:13 remaining. Allen's 35-yard pass to Kincaid moved the ball to the Houston 33 with 1:53 left. Three plays later, Allen connected with Palmer on a deep post with 1:36 remaining. A two-point pass failed. The Bills snapped a six-game losing streak in Houston. Buffalo hadn't won there since 2006 when J.P. Losman was the quarterback. Houston took a 28-27 lead when Stroud connected with Montgomery on a 7-yard scoring pass with 13:34 remaining in the game. The Bills regained the lead on Bass' 33-yard field goal with 10:31 left, but the Texans countered with Ka'imi Fairbairn's 58-yard field goal with 6:44 remaining. Allen rushed for two scores and passed for one as the Bills built a 24-21 halftime lead. After Bass opened the scoring with a 46-yard field goal midway through the first quarter, Montgomery scored from the 1 with 32 seconds left in the period. Allen avoided the rush and scampered 21 yards for a touchdown to give the Bills a 10-7 lead with 12:46 remaining in the second quarter. This time, Montgomery raced 18 yards to put Houston back ahead with 4:48 left. Allen scored from the 1 to give Buffalo a 17-14 lead with 3:59 remaining. After forcing a punt, the Bills went 96 yards on three plays as Allen hit Kincaid for 38 yards and Moore for 15 before tossing a 43-yard touchdown pass to Moore for a 10-point advantage with 1:29 left. The Texans responded with Stroud's 12-yard scoring strike to Collins with 26 seconds remaining. Buffalo increased its lead to 27-21 on Bass' 34-yard field goal with 4:24 left in the third quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Zimbabwe recall veterans Cremer and Taylor for Australia series
item.description: Zimbabwe have named Sikandar Raza as captain and recalled veteran players Graeme Cremer and Brendan Taylor for this week’s three-match One Day International series against Australia with skipper Richard Ngarava out injured.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zimbabwe have named Sikandar Raza as captain and recalled veteran players Graeme Cremer and Brendan Taylor for this week’s three-match One Day International series against Australia with skipper Richard Ngarava out injured. Ngarava has a lower-back injury and is one of three players from the squad that beat Bangladesh 2-1 in a home ODI series in July who will miss the Australia series. Veteran batsman Taylor, 40, returns to the ODI squad for the first time in a year and will help with wicketkeeping duties as Clive Madande is also injured. Graeme Cremer, who turns 40 on Saturday, has been recalled to help in the bowling department, more than two decades after he made his debut as a teenager. The leg spinner last played an ODI for Zimbabwe eight years ago but was in their Twenty20 side that competed in a tri-series with Namibia and South Africa in Windhoek earlier this month. Tanaka Chivanga, who is recovering from an Achilles tendon injury, is the other player from Zimbabwe’s most recent ODI series ruled out this week. Zimbabwe host Australia at Harare Sports Club on Tuesday, Friday, and Sunday. Squad: Sikandar Raza (captain), Ben Curran, Blessing Muzarabani, Brad Evans, Brendan Taylor, Brian Bennett, Craig Ervine, Ernest Masuku, Graeme Cremer, Innocent Kaia, Newman Nyamhuri, Ryan Burl, Tadiwanashe Marumani, Wellington Masakadza, and Wessly Madhevere.

item.title: Cam Schlittler dominant as Yankees shut out Mets
item.description: Cam Schlittler pitched six innings of one-hit ball in his latest stellar outing, and the host New York Yankees earned a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets in the final game of the Subway Series on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cam Schlittler pitched six innings of one-hit ball in his latest stellar outing, and the host New York Yankees earned a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets in the final game of the Subway Series on Sunday afternoon. Ben Rice and Austin Wells provided the only runs of the game via solo home runs as the Yankees (86-63) won for the 18th time in 26 games and lowered their magic number for clinching a postseason spot to one. Schlittler allowed only Brett Baty's double with two outs in the fifth. It was the third time in his 45 career starts that Schlittler allowed one hit and the second time this season. Schlittler struck out eight and walked two. He moved into a tie with Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski for the major league lead by lowering his ERA to 1.95 ERA. Schlittler threw 60 of 94 pitches for strikes and ended his outing after taking Bo Bichette's comebacker off the back of his right leg. The ball deflected to catcher Wells, who threw to Luis Garcia Jr. at first base to complete the out. Afterwards, Schlittler headed straight to the clubhouse but seemed fine. Rice slugged his third career leadoff homer and Wells homered in the third off Mets starter Christian Scott (4-5). Scott allowed two runs on three hits in six innings. The right-hander struck out Aaron Judge three times and finished with seven strikeouts to go with two walks. Judge went 0-for-3 and is 3-for-17 since being activated from the IL. The Yankees' Brent Headrick tossed a 1-2-3 seventh and Paul Blackburn got Lindor on a pop-up to end the eighth. David Bednar stranded a runner and notched his 34th save in 37 chances. The Mets (69-80) were blanked for the 14th time as Lindor and Juan Soto were a combined 0-for-7 with four strikeouts. --Field Level Media

item.title: T.J. Watt, Steelers stifle Falcons
item.description: Aaron Rodgers began his final NFL season by throwing for 221 yards and a score and T.J. Watt returned an interception for a touchdown to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 20-13 victory over the visiting Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Aaron Rodgers began his final NFL season by throwing for 221 yards and a score and T.J. Watt returned an interception for a touchdown to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 20-13 victory over the visiting Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Watt also had three tackles for loss and two sacks for the Steelers (1-0), who won their third straight season opener. Cooper Rush completed 12 of 22 passes for 143 yards and a touchdown while throwing two interceptions for the Falcons (0-1). Bijan Robinson rushed for 83 yards and had eight catches for 90 yards and a score. Facing a 13-7 halftime deficit, Atlanta threatened to cut the margin in half on its first drive of the second half, but Nick Folk missed his second field goal attempt of the game -- this time a 45-yard try. The Steelers punted and then turned the ball over on downs on their next two possessions. Robinson took a 24-yard pass into Pittsburgh territory on the next drive, which led to Folk's 51-yarder that trimmed the lead to 13-10 with 1:50 left in the third. After a Pittsburgh punt, Watt plucked Rush's pass out of the air and returned it 35 yards for a touchdown to make it 20-10 with 14:05 remaining in the fourth. The Falcons answered with Folk's 43-yarder, then Pittsburgh's Chris Boswell missed wide right on a 56-yard attempt to leave the door open for the visitors with 6:58 left. Atlanta advanced to the Steelers' 34 on the following possession, but Alex Highsmith sacked Rush to force a punt. Pittsburgh picked up three first downs on the final drive to ice the win. The Steelers struck first on Boswell's 43-yard field goal. Following the Falcons' second punt, Atlanta's Mike Hughes forced Jaylen Warren's fumble that was recovered at the Steelers' 25-yard line. Three plays later, Rush tossed a swing pass to Robinson, who took it 23 yards for a touchdown to give the Falcons a 7-3 edge with 1:13 left in the first quarter. Pittsburgh had to settle for another Boswell field goal on the ensuing drive, a 28-yarder to pull the Steelers within a point. Pittsburgh regained the ball when Rush was picked off by Jaquan Brisker. Rodgers then hit Warren for 18 yards before finding Pat Freiermuth for a 6-yard touchdown pass to give the Steelers a 13-7 edge. Folk then missed a 54-yard field goal try in his first attempt with Atlanta. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump dice que va a eliminar los aranceles de EEUU sobre el whisky irlandés
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el domingo, al término de su visita a Irlanda, que eliminaría el arancel del 10% sobre el whisky irlandés, que actualmente forma parte de los impuestos que gravan todas las exportaciones de vinos y bebidas espirituosas de la Unión Europea a Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el domingo, al término de su visita a Irlanda, que eliminaría el arancel del 10% sobre el whisky irlandés, que actualmente forma parte de los impuestos que gravan todas las exportaciones de vinos y bebidas espirituosas de la Unión Europea a Estados Unidos. Trump hizo el anuncio ante una multitud de aficionados irlandeses del golf en un torneo celebrado en un campo propiedad de su familia. Se reunió con el primer ministro irlandés, Micheal Martin, en Dublín el sábado, al inicio de una visita de 48 horas al país. "El Taoiseach (primer ministro de Irlanda) y yo hablamos de ello, y Shane (el golfista Shane Lowry) también lo mencionó, y todo el mundo me ha estado insistiendo diciendo: '¿Me harías un favor? Es muy injusto lo que está pasando. ¿Podrías eliminar los aranceles del whisky irlandés?'", explicó Trump. "Y les dije que, en nombre de los Estados Unidos de América, voy a eliminar los aranceles sobre el whisky irlandés", anunció entre los vítores de la multitud. Las exportaciones de vino y bebidas espirituosas a Estados Unidos se vieron afectadas por un arancel del 15% aplicado a la mayoría de los productos en virtud de un acuerdo comercial entre la UE y Estados Unidos alcanzado el año pasado. Los nuevos aranceles estadounidenses impuestos posteriormente en julio a 60 socios comerciales, incluida la UE, redujeron el tipo al 10%. La medida formaba parte de los esfuerzos por reconstruir el muro arancelario casi global de Trump después de que la Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos anuló sus aranceles iniciales. La Asociación Irlandesa del Whisky (IWA) acogió con satisfacción el anuncio y dijo que seguiría colaborando con sus homólogos de la UE y Estados Unidos para garantizar el retorno al acuerdo arancelario "cero por cero" para todas las exportaciones de bebidas. "Nada ejemplifica mejor la relación comercial entre Estados Unidos e Irlanda que el whisky irlandés", dijo el director de la IWA, Eoin O Caitin, en un comunicado, y añadió que el grupo de presión esperaba con interés que el anuncio se aplicara plenamente.

item.title: Bengals capitalize on clumsy Buccaneers' 4 fumbles to open '26 with win
item.description: CINCINNATI -- Cincinnati's overhauled defense converted three first-half fumbles into touchdowns and led the Bengals past the visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers 33-27 on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CINCINNATI -- Cincinnati's overhauled defense converted three first-half fumbles into touchdowns and led the Bengals past the visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers 33-27 on Sunday. Joe Burrow finished 25-of-35 for 254 yards, a touchdown and an interception for the Bengals (1-0), who finished with four forced turnovers. Baker Mayfield was 23-of-28 for 216 yards and a touchdown run for the Buccaneers (0-1), who dropped their first season opener since 2020. Mayfield lost three fumbles for the first time in his career. Evan McPherson converted all four field goal attempts, including kicks of 55 and 58 yards, to help Cincinnati to its first Week 1 win at home since beating Minnesota in 2021. The Bengals jumped out to a 24-10 halftime lead thanks to their defense. With Tampa Bay up 3-0, Mayfield was strip-sacked by Myles Murphy and Barrett Carter, with Murphy getting credit for the forced fumble. Demetrius Knight Jr. picked up the fumble and raced 27 yards for Cincinnati's first touchdown of the season. It was the first scoop-and-score for the Bengals since the "Fumble in the Jungle" in a January 2023 playoff game, when Sam Hubbard picked up Tyler Huntley's fumble and ran 98 yards for the touchdown in the playoff win over the Ravens. On the next possession, Bryan Cook forced a fumble from Bucky Irving and Boye Mafe recovered at the Tampa Bay 33. Given great field position, the offense finished it off with a touchdown throw of 2 yards to Mike Gesicki, who caught it at the 1 and fell backwards into the end zone for a 14-3 lead. Tampa Bay appeared to be getting ready to score as they marched into the red zone. But after eluding a heavy pass rush and dancing into open field at the 12, Mayfield ran up the middle. At the 4-yard line, Carter came in and forced the fumble. The ball rolled into the end zone, where it was recovered by Cook. The Bengals then marched 80 yards and made it 21-3 when Chase Brown ran 5 yards untouched up the middle for the touchdown. Momentum swung Tampa Bay's way with three minutes left in the third quarter when rookie Josiah Trotter intercepted Burrow and took it 38 yards to the house to cut Cincinnati's lead to 27-20. McPherson made two of his field goals in the fourth quarter (58 and 32 yards) to push the lead to 33-20. Mayfield's 9-yard scoring run came with 3:19 left, but the Buccaneers opted to kick it to Cincinnati and the Bengals were able to bleed the rest of the clock. --Mike Petraglia, Field Level Media

item.title: Jets WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) exit opener
item.description: New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. was ruled out for the remainder of their season opener Sunday at the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. was ruled out for the remainder of their season opener Sunday at the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury. Meanwhile, veteran safety Minkah Fitzpatrick injured his groin and was downgraded from questionable to doubtful during the second half. Cooper, selected in the first round (30th overall) in April's draft out of Indiana, caught his lone target for a 30-yard gain to set up a touchdown on the Jets' opening drive. Fitzpatrick is a five-time Pro Bowler and three-time first-team All-Pro beginning his first season with his third NFL team. He had 690 tackles, 21 interceptions, 60 pass breakups, six forced fumbles and seven recoveries in eight seasons for the Miami Dolphins (2018-19, 2025) and Pittsburgh Steelers (2019-24). --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets dominate Titans to ruin Robert Saleh's Tennessee debut
item.description: Kenyon Sadiq and Breece Hall ran for touchdowns, Geno Smith threw for 215 yards and the visiting New York Jets put the clamps on the Tennessee Titans to start the season with a 23-10 win on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kenyon Sadiq and Breece Hall ran for touchdowns, Geno Smith threw for 215 yards and the visiting New York Jets put the clamps on the Tennessee Titans to start the season with a 23-10 win on Sunday afternoon. Smith was 19 of 24 in winning his first start for the Jets (1-0) since 2016. Hall added 102 yards on 22 rushes as the Jets outgained Tennessee 367-195 and hogged the ball for 38 minutes and 46 seconds. Cam Ward struggled most of the game for the Titans (0-1), hitting 19 of 32 passes for only 140 yards and a late touchdown. Ward played under constant pressure as New York recorded three sacks and forced him into inaccurate throws. The outcome spoiled the first game for Robert Saleh as Tennessee's coach. The ex-Jets boss and his coaching staff got a glimpse of how much ground the team has to cover to be competitive in the AFC South, let alone against the league's top teams. The Jets wasted little time putting their stamp on the game, taking the opening kickoff and marching 60 yards in eight plays. Sadiq covered the last 3 yards on a tight end reverse, rumbling inside the left front pylon of the end zone at the 10:45 mark. Joey Slye connected on a 42-yard field goal with 5:03 left in the first quarter for the Titans. But Tennessee wouldn't score again until Ward found Elic Ayomanor for an 11-yard touchdown strike with 2:42 remaining in the game. Jason Sanders drilled a 33-yard field goal with 5:03 remaining in the second quarter to make it 10-3 New York. It capped a 19-play drive, 15 of them runs, that lasted a whopping 11:48. Hall upped the advantage to 17-3 with 9:41 left in the third quarter on a 4-yard run that finished an 80-yard drive. Smith fueled it with completions of 31 and 40 yards to Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, respectively. Sanders added a 51-yard field goal with 4:33 remaining in the period and a 52-yarder with five minutes left in the game --Field Level Media

item.title: Trevor Lawrence (4 TDs), Jaguars blitz Browns 34-10
item.description: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes and the Jaguars dominated the Cleveland Browns with a 34-10 win Sunday in Jacksonville.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes and the Jaguars dominated the Cleveland Browns with a 34-10 win Sunday in Jacksonville. Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 245 yards as Jacksonville built a 31-0 lead before tapping the brakes in the second half. Parker Washington caught Lawrence's first TD pass and led the Jaguars with five receptions for 83 yards. Ten Jacksonville receivers caught at least one pass. Jacksonville opened the second half with an easy four-play touchdown drive, covering 60 yards in under three minutes before Lawrence and Jakobi Meyers hooked up on a 32-yard scoring strike for a 31-0 lead. The Browns escaped the shutout on the next possession but spoiled a 74-yard kickoff return by Raheim Sanders, going just 15 yards on seven plays before Andre Szmyt's 26-yard field goal. Deshaun Watson threw a 46-yard TD pass to rookie Denzel Boston with 1:52 remaining in the game. Watson was 16 of 22 for 205 yards and an interception, with rookies Boston and KC Concepcion accounting for six catches and 102 yards. Already trailing 14-0, Watson recovered his own fumble as Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen converged on him in the pocket as the first quarter came to an end. But the Jaguars just kept scoring. The ensuing drive ended in a field goal. After the Jaguars recovered Concepcion's fumble, Lawrence tallied his third TD pass of the game with 6:18 left in the second quarter. The 14-yarder to tight end Brenton Strange gave Jacksonville a 24-0 lead. Watson's third pass attempt of the game was picked off by Foyesade Oluokun and set up the first Jacksonville touchdown. Washington made a diving, two-handed grab for a 30-yard TD pass to open the scoring in the first quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: USA overcome 14-point deficit, beat France 97-79 to win Women's World Cup
item.description: Defending champions USA fell behind early but stormed back past France 97-79 on Sunday to win the Women's World Cup.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Defending champions USA fell behind early but stormed back past France 97-79 on Sunday to win the Women's World Cup. In a rematch of the 2024 Olympic Games final, the American women came out on top once more, earning their fifth consecutive World Cup title and stretching their impressive unbeaten run at Olympics or World Cups to 20 years. The French had to settle for silver in their maiden World Cup final appearance for their best ever finish, despite leading by 14 points at one stage. USA captain Breanna Stewart, top scorer with 22 points, helped her team carve out an early five-point lead, anchoring the scoring early on. But the French exploded into action, quickly found their three-point range and, led by Gabby Williams, went on a 21-2 rampage that saw them open up a 14-point advantage early in the second quarter. The Americans started chipping away at the lead and trailed by just two points at the break after Caitlin Clark hit a massively important three-pointer at the buzzer. Consecutive triples from Kahleah Copper and Jackie Young gave Team USA a 58-51 lead and they never looked back, with another Clark three-pointer stretching their lead to 19 points at the start of the fourth quarter. The French could not break past a hard-working defence. Earlier on Sunday, Spain secured the bronze medal, outclassing hosts Germany 81-58 in the match for third place.

item.title: La china Z.AI recauda 5.000 millones de dólares con venta de nuevas acciones, bonos convertibles: documento
item.description: La empresa de inteligencia artificial Z.AI Co Ltd, con sede en Pekín, recaudó un total de 5.000 millones de dólares mediante una colocación de acciones en Hong Kong por valor de unos 2.000 millones de dólares y una venta simultánea de bonos convertibles por valor de unos 3.000 millones de dólares, informó la firma el domingo en un comunicado a la Bolsa de Hong Kong.
item.dc:creator: Kane Wu
item.content:encoded: La empresa de inteligencia artificial Z.AI Co Ltd, con sede en Pekín, recaudó un total de 5.000 millones de dólares mediante una colocación de acciones en Hong Kong por valor de unos 2.000 millones de dólares y una venta simultánea de bonos convertibles por valor de unos 3.000 millones de dólares, informó la firma el domingo en un comunicado a la Bolsa de Hong Kong. Z.AI (2513.HK) lanzó las ventas el viernes, ofreciendo 21,97 millones de nuevas acciones en Hong Kong a 714 dólares de Hong Kong (91,05 dólares) cada una, lo que supone un descuento del 10% respecto al precio de cierre del viernes, que fue de 793 dólares de Hong Kong. La empresa también recaudó 20.140 millones de yuanes (3.000 millones de dólares) mediante bonos cupón cero con vencimiento en septiembre de 2027, según se desprende del comunicado. Los bonos denominados en yuanes se liquidarán en dólares estadounidenses. Según el documento presentado, los bonos se emitieron al 100,5% de su valor nominal. El precio de conversión inicial es de 892,50 dólares de Hong Kong, lo que supone una prima del 25% respecto al precio de colocación de las acciones de 714 dólares de Hong Kong. Z.AI podrá amortizar la totalidad de los bonos, pero no una parte de ellos, a partir del 18 de febrero de 2027, si sus acciones cotizan a un precio igual o superior al 130% del precio de conversión durante 20 de los 30 días de negociación, según la documentación. Alrededor del 60% de los ingresos netos se destinará a la investigación y el desarrollo de los modelos de próxima generación de la empresa y de su sistema de autoaprendizaje completo, según indicó Z.AI en el documento. Otro 15% de los ingresos se destinará a los planes de expansión de la empresa, mientras que el resto se utilizará para optimizar su estructura de capital, reponer el capital circulante para las operaciones diarias y para otros fines corporativos generales, según el documento. La recaudación de fondos se produce en un momento en que los desarrolladores chinos de IA buscan capital para la costosa infraestructura informática y el talento necesarios para competir con sus rivales estadounidenses de mayor envergadura. Z.AI, anteriormente conocida como Zhipu AI, salió a bolsa en Hong Kong en enero y recaudó unos 4.000 millones de dólares en una venta de acciones posterior realizada en julio.

item.title: Russell says he is not realistically in the fight for F1 title
item.description: George Russell said he was no longer a realistic Formula One title contender despite being the closest challenger to Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: George Russell said he was no longer a realistic Formula One title contender despite being the closest challenger to Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli. Antonelli's Spanish Grand Prix victory in Madrid on Sunday left the Briton 81 points adrift of the Italian after 14 rounds. The win was 20-year-old Antonelli's eighth of the season, one more than Russell, 28, has managed in a career that started with Williams in 2019. Depending on what[USN:L6N4530U3 TEXT:" happens in the Middle East,"] with the season supposed to end in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, there are either nine rounds remaining or eight if Italy's Imola circuit -- the closest to Antonelli's hometown Bologna -- replaces the Gulf races as many expect to happen. That means there is a maximum of 233 points still to be won, including a sprint race in Singapore. "We’re obviously in a great place to win the constructors’," Russell said after finishing fifth on Sunday. "Realistically, I’m not in the fight for the drivers’, and that just allows me to focus race by race and try to get some good results." Russell was the title favourite, according to bookmakers, before the season started but has won only two races this season. Mercedes are 145 points clear of second-placed Ferrari.

item.title: Solberg wins in Chile as Toyota secure sixth manufacturers' title in a row
item.description: Oliver Solberg won Rally Chile on Sunday as Toyota clinched the manufacturers' world championship for the sixth time in a row and record-equalling 10th.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oliver Solberg won Rally Chile on Sunday as Toyota clinched the manufacturers' world championship for the sixth time in a row and record-equalling 10th. Solberg beat nine-time world champion teammate Sebastien Ogier by 16.6 seconds with Adrien Fourmaux third for Hyundai, 33.3 seconds off the pace. It was the Swede's first win since Monte Carlo at the start of the campaign and he ended the weekend with a haul of 34 points. "It has been an up and down year but the team always supported and believed," he said. The podium was Ogier's 120th in the world championship, putting him level with fellow-French great Sebastien Loeb. Toyota had needed only seven points to retain the title and wrapped it up with two rounds to spare, now on 614 points to Hyundai's 410, and are level with Lancia in the record books for total titles. Welshman Elfyn Evans had been second overnight but finished fifth after having to change a wheel on the penultimate stage, losing more than two minutes and having his championship lead cut to 17 points. “We did what we could. Of course it was looking pretty positive this morning, but these things happen. We keep at it,” he said. He made sure of bonus points by setting the second-fastest time, beaten only by Solberg, on the final Wolf Power Stage and now has 230 points to teammate Sami Pajari's 213 and Solberg's 209. Pajari closed the gap to Evans by finishing fourth. The next race is the Italian round in Sardinia from October 1-4, with the finale scheduled for Saudi Arabia in November.

item.title: Basket/Coupe du monde-Les Bleues battues en finale par les USA
item.description: L'équipe de France féminine de basket s'est inclinée dimanche en finale de la Coupe du monde face aux États-Unis (97-79), victorieuses de leur cinquième titre consécutif, et a conclu la compétition avec l'argent, le meilleur résultat de son histoire après l'unique médaille de bronze obtenue en 1953.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'équipe de France féminine de basket s'est inclinée dimanche en finale de la Coupe du monde face aux États-Unis (97-79), victorieuses de leur cinquième titre consécutif, et a conclu la compétition avec l'argent, le meilleur résultat de son histoire après l'unique médaille de bronze obtenue en 1953. Deux ans après leur cruelle défaite d'un point en finale des Jeux olympiques de Paris 2024 (67-66), les Françaises n'ont pas démérité face aux Américaines, lauréates de leur 12e titre mondial et toujours invaincues en grande compétition depuis 2006, avant de sombrer après la pause. Les Bleues ont dominé en première période, comptant jusqu'à 14 unités d'avance en début de deuxième quart-temps grâce à leur défense et leur adresse (31-17), symbolisée par leur capitaine Gabby Williams (20 points, dont 16 en première période). Mais les États-Unis sont revenus progressivement afin d'atteindre la mi-temps avec seulement deux points de retard (45-43). Le troisième quart-temps a ensuite été fatal aux joueuses de Jean-Aimé Toupane, qui ont encaissé un 30 à 12 au retour des vestiaires. Menées de 16 points à l'entame des dix dernières minutes (57-73), le défi était trop grand pour les Tricolores puisque l'écart a même atteint 27 unités à six minutes du buzzer final (86-59). Un an après leur décevante quatrième place à l'Euro, soit leur pire résultat continental depuis 2007, les Bleues ont toutefois réalisé un parcours presque parfait, à deux ans des Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles. Portées par leur huit joueuses (sur 12) de WNBA, la ligue nord-américaine, elles ont conclu invaincues le premier tour, écartant facilement la Hongrie (99-53), la Corée du Sud (95-69) et le Nigeria (111-56). Dans la phase à élimination directe, l'équipe de France avait ensuite battu la Chine en quarts de finale (90-61) pour briser son plafond de verre des six dernières éditions avant d'écarter samedi l'Allemagne (86-64), qui évoluait pourtant à domicile, à Berlin.
